blocks.text: To do the same work many times you use a **loop**. `for i in 0..5:` runs the indented part five times, with `i` being 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (5 is not included).
A `while` loop keeps running as long as the condition is true. If you forget to make it false at some point, the loop never ends!
`n -= 1` is short for `n = n - 1`; `+=` increases in the same way.

blocks.prompt: Add up the numbers from 1 to 5 and print the total. (`1..=5` includes both 1 and 5.)

blocks.q: How many times does `for i in 0..3:` run?
